studies.censoring: Source-reported Table 1 means and SDs; no invented individual observations.
studies.overlap: 181 Vietnamese landraces and three reference genotypes; brown and white grain share plants. Genotypes and technical repeats are not independent studies.
studies.limitations: Experimental genotype collection in one field setting; not a national market distribution. Total arsenic was measured without speciation.
studies.verification_basis: Existing canonical Table 1 extraction retained; primary material, paired-grain design and 184-genotype composition checked. Not a new sample-level extraction.

comparison_design.context: Same-plant brown and white grain from 184 genotypes in one field study; source-reported rounded means. No individual paired differences, uncertainty for the contrast or statistical significance are inferred. Equal rounded means do not establish equivalence.

studies.region_type: Purchase market; origins and processing differ by category
studies.basis: FDA 45 g dry-weight rice serving; rounded average converted to µg/kg dry weight
studies.method: FDA arsenic speciation survey; summary category averages, including specified substitutions
studies.locator: Summary Table: printed page 1 (PDF page 2); rice serving basis: printed page 12 (PDF page 13), footnote 2; full rice analytical results and LOD/LOQ appendix
studies.censoring: Summary averages use half total arsenic when samples were not speciated, and half the detection limit when total arsenic was below detection. No new zero or sample-level values are imputed.
studies.overlap: The September 2013 release includes September 2012 samples. Category rows are reused within this one survey, not independent studies; mixed Other category excluded.
studies.limitations: Different retail products in the same historical FDA survey, with unequal sample counts and mixed origins. Basmati and jasmine categories include both brown and white products; preparation also varies. These are descriptive category averages, not matched grains, a cultivar effect, statistical significance or a current sourcing guarantee. FDA used substitutions for some non-speciated or non-detected samples. Rounded original averages are converted using the stated 45 g dry-rice serving; conversion adds no measurement precision.
studies.verification_basis: Original FDA PDF summary, rice-serving footnote and analytical-table dry-weight headers verified on 2026-10-19; no new sample register or inferential analysis.

comparison_design.context: Different retail products in the same historical FDA survey, with unequal sample counts and mixed origins.
